problem: Let ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ be eigenvectors of a matrix $A.$ Find the decoupling matrix of the differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$
worked_solution:
First, we construct the matrix $E$, whose columns are the eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}:$

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 5 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, the decoupling matrix can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={E}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 5 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\cdot 3-5\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
